newsitem.title: FRANCE: French government slams G7 summits as useless.
newsitem.headline: French government slams G7 summits as useless.

text.p: French Foreign Minister Hubert Vedrine says that G7 summits have become giant "media circuses" which serve no purpose in making decisions on crucial issues and have outlived their usefulness.

"The G7 summits have become a gigantic media circus, which stand out for the absence of any real working meetings," Vedrine said following last weekend's Group of Seven Denver summit, according to the French National Assembly's Committee on Foreign Affairs.
"In general, these summits only formulate resolutions full of empty rhetoric and stripped of decisions," he said according to a committee statement.
The statement summarising closed-door testimony delivered by Vedrine on Thursday was released by the parliamentary panel on Friday.
In his testimony, Vedrine also stepped up a French attack on U.S. "hegemony" at the Denver summit, saying that Washington had irritated all participants at the meeting of industrialised powers.
"The Denver summit was different from previous meetings in the unprecedented arrogance of the tone of American statements. All the participants were irritated," Vedrine said.
Earlier in the week, Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin had also accused the United States of hegemony in seeking to impose its economic and social model on Europe at the summit.

"I am not satisfied with the results of Denver," Jospin told parliament. "We see a certain tendency towards hegemony, which is not necessarily identical with exercising the global responsibilities of a great power, even if it is a friend."
Jospin did not attend the Denver summit, leaving conservative President Jacques Chirac to represent France.

The French media have provided overwhelmingly negative coverage of the summit, accusing President Bill Clinton of cowboy arrogance in lecturing Europe on jobs and growth when the United States had greater inequality, worse poverty, poorer social services and more violent crime than western European nations.

The media were particularly scornful of Clinton's request that G7 leaders don cowboy boots and Stetson hats for a G7 dinner, interpreting the incident as a symbol of America's will to impose its model on a reluctant Europe.
Vedrine's and Jospin's statements reflect a longtime bipartisan consensus in France that Paris should resist U.S. dominance.
But Vedrine's remarks on the G7 meeting go farther than previous comments on the regular get-togethers by the United States, Japan, France, Germany, Britain, Canada and Italy.
Russia has also attended recent G7 meetings, though not as a full member.
